title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Ten documented Coast Guard Academy customs, ceremonies, and objects that mark cadet life from Swab Summer through commissioning.

cards.title: 100th Day role reversal
cards.subtitle: Fourth Class Cadets take the lead for a day
cards.notes: Look for Academy coverage around 100 days before graduation; the custom briefly reverses parts of the fourth- and second-class routine.
cards.short_summary: A calendar-marked reversal of cadet hierarchy.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy says that, typically 100 days before graduation, Fourth Class Cadets become “kings for a day” while Second Class Cadets obey their commands.
cards.access_notes: A cadet tradition; confirm any public observation options with the Academy calendar.

cards.title: The class ring arrives in April
cards.subtitle: A signet ring with Academy and class crests
cards.notes: Notice the Academy crest and individual class crest on the signet ring, then connect it to the later Ring Dance christening.
cards.short_summary: A wearable cadet symbol that stays with alumni.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy states that Second Class Cadets receive the signet ring in April; it bears the Academy crest and the individual’s class crest.
cards.access_notes: A personal cadet item; view only when displayed publicly or by invitation.

cards.title: A photo tucked into the cover
cards.subtitle: Cadets personalize the inside of a uniform hat
cards.notes: If a cadet chooses to show you their cover, ask about the photo inside; the Academy identifies this as a tradition for loved ones.
cards.short_summary: A private personal detail inside a formal uniform item.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy says it is tradition for cadets to place a picture of a loved one or someone special in their combination cover.
cards.access_notes: Personal uniform item; do not handle or photograph without the owner’s permission.

cards.title: Two silver dollars at commissioning
cards.subtitle: One for the Anchor Cadet and one for a first salute
cards.notes: Watch commencement coverage for the silver-dollar custom and the moment loved ones commonly place new ensigns’ shoulder boards.
cards.short_summary: A commissioning ritual built around two pocketed coins.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy says graduating ensigns carry two silver dollars: one for the Anchor Cadet and one for the first person to render a salute.
cards.access_notes: Occurs during commencement; follow Academy visitor guidance for attendance.

cards.title: The Chase Hall words no one steps on
cards.subtitle: “Who Lives Here Reveres Honor, Honors Duty”
cards.notes: Find the inlaid Quarterdeck words in Chase Hall and observe the custom respectfully; do not step on the inscription.
cards.short_summary: An inlaid phrase treated as a physical symbol of the Honor Concept.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy identifies the words inlaid on the Quarterdeck of Chase Hall as a symbol of honor and says they should never be tread upon.
cards.access_notes: Chase Hall access may be restricted; follow posted access rules and Academy instructions.

cards.title: Ring the black buoy for luck
cards.subtitle: The navigational buoy by the museum
cards.notes: Locate the black navigational buoy by the museum and treat it gently; Academy tradition associates ringing it with good luck.
cards.short_summary: A buoy turned into a campus luck ritual.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy states that tradition holds a cadet who rings the black navigational buoy by the museum will be granted good luck.
cards.access_notes: Confirm campus and museum-area access before visiting; respect the object and surrounding grounds.

cards.title: Dress the bear before game day
cards.subtitle: The Academy mascot stands behind Chase Hall
cards.notes: See whether Objee is dressed for an upcoming game or event, and photograph the statue only from publicly accessible grounds.
cards.short_summary: A black-bear mascot statue that changes outfits for campus spirit.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy says Objee is its black-bear mascot and that the statue behind Chase Hall is commonly dressed up for major events and athletic games.
cards.access_notes: Located in the park behind Chase Hall; comply with campus visitor and photography rules.

cards.title: Christen a class ring with seven oceans
cards.subtitle: A Saturday-before-graduation rite at the Ring Monument
cards.notes: Follow official Graduation Week information for this formal event; the ring’s seven-oceans christening is the central documented ritual.
cards.short_summary: A formal transition toward first-class year.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy says that at Ring Dance, each couple proceeds to the Ring Monument and the escort dips the ring into water from the world’s seven oceans.
cards.access_notes: Held during Graduation Week; attendance and access are determined by Academy event guidance.

cards.title: The end of being a Swab
cards.subtitle: Upper-class cadets pin on Fourth Class shoulder boards
cards.notes: Watch for the Crown Park ceremony before classes begin, when former Swabs formally enter the Corps of Cadets.
cards.short_summary: A visible handoff from Swab Summer to cadet status.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy states that, at the end of Swab Summer, upper-class cadets affix Fourth Class shoulder boards on former Swabs in a Crown Park ceremony.
cards.access_notes: Occurs before classes start; check Academy communications for any visitor arrangements.

cards.title: Find out the first Coast Guard assignment
cards.subtitle: First Class Cadets learn their initial billets together
cards.notes: Look for official Billet Night coverage to see the annual reveal, when graduating cadets learn their first Coast Guard assignments.
cards.short_summary: An annual career-reveal ceremony for the senior class.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy describes Billet Night as an annual tradition in which First Class Cadets learn where they will go for their first Coast Guard assignment.
cards.access_notes: An Academy event; public attendance is not stated on the cited page.
